question: Can a continual topic model that carries a prior forward across time slices beat a sequential online LDA baseline on topic coherence and topic stability over a text stream?
method: Stratified 80/20 split of 20 Newsgroups; training part cut into 5 random time slices; sequential online LDA (20 topics) vs the same LDA with 50/50 mixing of the previous topic-word matrix before each slice; evaluated by NPMI on held-out test docs, stability and LR macro-F1; 3 seeds.
metric_name: NPMI topic coherence of top-10 words on held-out test documents
baseline: Standard sequential online LDA (sklearn LatentDirichletAllocation, partial_fit per slice, 20 topics); stand-in, not the paper's neural CoNTM.
improved: Same online LDA, but before each new slice the previous topic-word matrix is mixed 50/50 with the current slice's topic-word estimate as a continual global prior.
notes: Topic stability compares index-aligned topics across consecutive slices. The improved model does an extra 5-iteration LDA fit per slice, so its compute is not identical to the baseline. No hyper-parameter search was run; all settings were fixed a priori. The 20 Newsgroups data has no timestamps, so random slices simulate a stream. Results are from a small seed count and a single data split.
